**Samuel M. Raimi**[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-first-4) ([/ˈ r eɪ m i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_RAY-mee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born October 23, 1959) is an American filmmaker. He is best known for writing and directing the [_Evil Dead_ trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil_Dead "Evil Dead") (1981–1993) and directing the [_Spider-Man_ trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man_in_film#Sam_Raimi's_trilogy "Spider-Man in film") (2002–2007). He also directed _[Darkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkman "Darkman")_ (1990), _[The Quick and the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quick\_and\_the\_Dead\_(1995\_film) "The Quick and the Dead (1995 film)")_ (1995), _[A Simple Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Simple\_Plan\_(film) "A Simple Plan (film)")_ (1998), _[The Gift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gift\_(2000\_film) "The Gift (2000 film)")_ (2000), _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_ (2009), _[Oz the Great and Powerful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_the\_Great\_and\_Powerful "Oz the Great and Powerful")_ (2013), _[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_in\_the\_Multiverse\_of\_Madness "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness")_ (2022) and _[Send Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Send\_Help "Send Help")_ (2026).

His films are known for their highly dynamic visual style, inspired by comic books and slapstick comedy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-6) He founded the production companies Renaissance Pictures in 1979 and [Ghost House Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_House_Pictures "Ghost House Pictures") in 2002. Raimi has also produced several successful television series, including _[Hercules: The Legendary Journeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hercules:\_The\_Legendary\_Journeys "Hercules: The Legendary Journeys")_ (1995–1997), its spin-off _[Xena: Warrior Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xena:\_Warrior\_Princess "Xena: Warrior Princess")_ (1995–2001), and _[Ash vs Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ash\_vs\_Evil\_Dead "Ash vs Evil Dead")_ (2015–2018) starring longtime friend and collaborator [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell") reprising his role in the _Evil Dead_ franchise.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Raimi was born on October 23, 1959, in [Royal Oak, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan"), a suburb of [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-TCM-1) His family was [Conservative Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Jewish "Conservative Jewish").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-7) He is a son of merchants Celia Barbara (née Abrams) (1929–2016) and Leonard Ronald Raimi (1926–2021).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-FilmRef-2) His ancestors were Jewish immigrants from Russia and Hungary.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-JewishJournal-March2012-8) His younger brother [Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Raimi "Ted Raimi") is an actor,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-9) and his older brother [Ivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Raimi "Ivan Raimi") is a screenwriter and physician.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-JewishJournal-March2012-8) His older sister, Andrea Raimi Rubin, is a court reporter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-10) Another older brother, Sander, died at 15 in an accidental drowning in [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"); Raimi has said that the trauma knitted the remaining family closer together and "colored everything he's done for the rest of his life."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-11) Raimi also mentioned that Sander first introduced him to _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man")_, igniting his love for comics.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-:0-12)

Raimi graduated from [Groves High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groves_High_School_(Michigan) "Groves High School (Michigan)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-macomb-13) and later went on to attend [Michigan State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_University "Michigan State University") and later [Università Bocconi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bocconi_University "Bocconi University") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), Italy,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-15) where he studied English but left after three semesters to film _[The Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Dead "The Evil Dead")_.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Film")]

Raimi became fascinated with making films when his father brought a movie camera home one day. He began to make [Super 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_8_mm_film "Super 8 mm film") movies with his friend [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell"), whom he met in 1975. In college, he collaborated with his brother's roommate [Robert Tapert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Tapert "Robert Tapert") and Campbell to shoot _[Within the Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Within\_the\_Woods "Within the Woods")_ (1979), a 32-minute horror film which raised $375,000, as well as his debut feature film _[It's Murder!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Murder! "It's Murder!")_. During that time, he also shot the seven-minute short film _Clockwork_ (1979), starring [Scott Spiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Spiegel "Scott Spiegel") (who had appeared in _Within the Woods_) and Cheryl Guttridge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-17) Through family, friends, and a network of investors, Raimi was able to finance production of the highly successful [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Dead "The Evil Dead")_ (1981), which became a cult hit and effectively launched Raimi's career.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-18)

He began work on his third film _[Crimewave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimewave "Crimewave")_ (1985), which he co-wrote with the then-unknown [Coen brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coen_brothers "Coen brothers"), shortly after.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-19) Intended as a live-action comic book, the film was unsuccessful, partly due to unwanted studio intervention. Raimi then returned to the horror genre with the seminal _[Evil Dead II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil\_Dead\_II "Evil Dead II")_ (which added [slapstick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick "Slapstick") humor to the over-the-top horror, showcasing his love of the [Three Stooges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Stooges "Three Stooges")). With his brother [Ivan Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Raimi "Ivan Raimi") (and crediting himself as Celia Abrams), Sam Raimi also wrote _[Easy Wheels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easy\_Wheels "Easy Wheels")_ (1989), which parodied the [Outlaw biker film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_biker_film "Outlaw biker film") genre. A long-time comic book buff, he then attempted to adapt "[The Shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shadow "The Shadow")" into a movie but was unable to secure the rights, so he created his own superhero, _[Darkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkman "Darkman")_ (1990). The film was his first [major studio picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_film_studio "Major film studio"), and was commercially successful, spawning two sequels. Through it he was still able to secure funding for _Evil Dead III_, which was retitled _[Army of Darkness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army\_of\_Darkness "Army of Darkness")_ and largely steered away from horror towards [fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film") and [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film") elements. _Army of Darkness_, the final movie in the _Evil Dead_ trilogy, commercially underperformed, yet on video became a cult classic.

In the 1990s, Raimi moved into other genres, directing such films as the western _[The Quick and the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quick\_and\_the\_Dead\_(1995\_film) "The Quick and the Dead (1995 film)")_ (starring [Sharon Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Stone "Sharon Stone") and [Gene Hackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Hackman "Gene Hackman")), the highly acclaimed crime thriller _[A Simple Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Simple\_Plan\_(film) "A Simple Plan (film)")_ (1998) (starring [Bill Paxton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Paxton "Bill Paxton") and [Billy Bob Thornton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Bob_Thornton "Billy Bob Thornton")), and the romantic drama _[For Love of the Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_Love\_of\_the\_Game\_(film) "For Love of the Game (film)")_ (1999) (starring [Kevin Costner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Costner "Kevin Costner")).

Raimi has frequently collaborated with [Joel and Ethan Coen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coen_brothers "Coen brothers"), beginning when Joel was one of the editors of _Evil Dead_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-20) The Coens co-wrote _Crimewave_ and _[The Hudsucker Proxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hudsucker\_Proxy "The Hudsucker Proxy")_ with Raimi in the mid-1980s (though _Hudsucker_ was not produced for almost a decade). Raimi made cameo appearances in _[Miller's Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miller's\_Crossing "Miller's Crossing")_, _The Hudsucker Proxy_, and with Joel Coen in _[Spies Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spies\_Like\_Us "Spies Like Us")_. The Coen brothers gave Raimi advice on shooting in snow for _A Simple Plan_, based on their experiences with _[Fargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo\_(1996\_film) "Fargo (1996 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-21)

Raimi has worked in front of the camera in _[The Stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Stand\_(1994\_miniseries) "The Stand (1994 miniseries)")_ as a dimwitted hitman, [John Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carpenter "John Carpenter")'s _[Body Bags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body\_Bags\_(film) "Body Bags (film)")_ as a murdered gas station attendant, and _[Indian Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Summer\_(1993\_film) "Indian Summer (1993 film)")_ in what is perhaps his biggest role as a bumbling assistant to [Alan Arkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Arkin "Alan Arkin"). The film was written by his childhood friend, writer-director [Mike Binder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Binder "Mike Binder"), and shot at the camp that they both attended when they were younger.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_%282%29.jpg/250px-Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_(2).jpg)

Raimi in 2007

Raimi achieved great critical and commercial success with the [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)")_[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ (2002), which was adapted from the comic book series [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man"). The movie grossed over US$800 million worldwide, spawning two sequels: _[Spider-Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_2 "Spider-Man 2")_ and _[Spider-Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_3 "Spider-Man 3")_, both directed by Raimi and each grossing approximately $800 million. After the completion of the third _Spider-Man_ film, he planned on producing two more sequels (although [Sony Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures "Sony Pictures") planned three sequels) but could not find a satisfactory script.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-rolling_stone-22) In 2022, reflecting on _Spider-Man 3_, Raimi told _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_: "It was a very painful experience for me. I wanted to make a Spider-Man movie to redeem myself for that. [The aborted] _Spider-Man 4_ — that was really what that was about. I wanted to go out on a high note. I didn't want to just make another one that pretty much worked. I had a really high standard in my mind. And I didn't think I could get that script to the level that I was hoping for by that start date."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-:0-12) He, along with [Marc Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Webb "Marc Webb"), were both brought on as creative consultants for [Marvel Studios'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios")_[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_, directed by [Jon Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Watts "Jon Watts").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-23)

Raimi produced the entire English-language [_The Grudge_ franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grudge_(film_series) "The Grudge (film series)"), based on the original Japanese films. On December 11, 2006, the website SuperHeroHype reported that director Sam Raimi and Michael Uslan would co-produce a new film version of _[The Shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shadow "The Shadow")_ for [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-24) On October 16, 2007, Raimi stated that: "I don't have any news on _The Shadow_ at this time, except that the company that I have with Josh Donen, my producing partner, we've got the rights to _The Shadow_. I love the character very much and we're trying to work on a story that'll do justice to the character."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-26) According to _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_, Raimi had expressed an interest in directing a film version of _[The Hobbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hobbit "The Hobbit")_, the prequel to the _[Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lord\_of\_the\_Rings "The Lord of the Rings")_ trilogy.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-27) In 2008, it was reported [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro") would direct with [Peter Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jackson "Peter Jackson") as the executive producer, though Jackson ultimately directed [_The Hobbit_ film series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hobbit_(film_series) "The Hobbit (film series)"). In 2008, it was reported Raimi might direct _By Any Means Necessary_, the next film based on the "Jack Ryan" CIA character created by [Tom Clancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Clancy "Tom Clancy") for [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-28) Disney also approached him to direct _[W.I.T.C.H.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W.I.T.C.H. "W.I.T.C.H."): The Movie_, based on the popular comic.

Raimi directed the horror film _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_, released in 2009 to critical acclaim.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-29) Blizzard Entertainment announced on July 22, 2009, that Raimi would be directing a film adaptation of the _[Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft "Warcraft")_ video game series,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-30) but at the 2012 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con"), it was revealed that he would not be the director.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-31)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg/250px-Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg)

Raimi (far left) at the _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_ film discussion panel at the 2008 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

In 2009, it was reported Raimi would produce the British [supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural "Supernatural")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_film "Thriller film")_Refuge_, which would be directed by [Corin Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corin_Hardy "Corin Hardy") and published by [Mandate Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_Pictures "Mandate Pictures"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-32) and the remake of the Danish thriller _[The Substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Substitute\_(2007\_film) "The Substitute (2007 film)")_, which would be directed by [Scott Derrickson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Derrickson "Scott Derrickson"), under his new label Spooky Pictures.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-33) In 2010, it was reported he would produce the British thriller flick _Burst 3D_ with his company [Ghost House Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_House_Pictures "Ghost House Pictures"), directed by [Neil Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Marshall "Neil Marshall").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-34)

Raimi directed _[Oz the Great and Powerful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_the\_Great\_and\_Powerful "Oz the Great and Powerful")_, which was released on March 8, 2013, by [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures") and grossed $493 million worldwide.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-36) He said he would not be directing the planned sequel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-signed-sequel-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-noraimi-38)

Raimi, along with Bruce Campbell and [Rob Tapert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Tapert "Rob Tapert"), produced 2013's _[Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil\_Dead\_(2013\_film) "Evil Dead (2013 film)"),_ a remake of Raimi's original film. First-time feature filmmaker [Fede Álvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fede_%C3%81lvarez "Fede Álvarez") wrote and directed, and [Diablo Cody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diablo_Cody "Diablo Cody") was also brought in to revise/rewrite the script.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-39) Raimi confirmed plans to write _Evil Dead 4_ with his brother; it was later specified that this film would be _Army of Darkness 2_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-40) Álvarez revealed that Raimi would direct the sequel to _Army of Darkness_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-41) However, in a 2014 interview, [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell") announced that _Army of Darkness 2_ is not happening, saying "It's all internet b.s. There's no reality whatsoever. These random comments slip out of either my mouth, or Sam Raimi's mouth, next thing you know, we're making a sequel."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-42)

Raimi speaking at the 2014 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

On February 26, 2016, it was confirmed that Raimi was attached to direct the upcoming film _World War 3_ for [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") The film would be based on a possible future inspired by the book _[The Next 100 Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Next\_100\_Years "The Next 100 Years")_ by [George Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Friedman "George Friedman").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-43) On February 16, 2017, it was reported that Raimi would be directing a thriller about the [Bermuda Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_Triangle "Bermuda Triangle") for [Skydance Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skydance_Media "Skydance Media"), with the script being written by Doug Miro and Carlo Bernard.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-44) By January 29, 2018, Raimi was set to direct the first in the movie adaptations of [Patrick Rothfuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Rothfuss "Patrick Rothfuss")'s [Kingkiller Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kingkiller_Chronicle "The Kingkiller Chronicle") series, _[The Name of the Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Name\_of\_the\_Wind "The Name of the Wind")_, with Rothfuss and [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") serving as executive producers.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-45)

On February 5, 2020, it was announced that Raimi was in talks with [Marvel Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios") to direct _[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_in\_the\_Multiverse\_of\_Madness "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness")_,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-46) and Raimi confirmed his involvement in April 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-47) This marked Raimi's return to the superhero film genre after more than 15 years following _Spider-Man 3_ in 2007 and his first feature film directorial effort since 2013's _Oz the Great and Powerful._[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-48)

Raimi next directed the horror-thriller film _[Send Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Send\_Help "Send Help")_, starring [Rachel McAdams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_McAdams "Rachel McAdams") and [Dylan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_O'Brien "Dylan O'Brien").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-49) The film was released in theatres by [20th Century Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on January 30, 2026.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-50)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Television")]

In addition to film, Raimi has worked in television, producing such series as _[Hercules: The Legendary Journeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hercules:\_The\_Legendary\_Journeys "Hercules: The Legendary Journeys")_ and its [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")_[Xena: Warrior Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xena:\_Warrior\_Princess "Xena: Warrior Princess")_, both featuring his younger brother [Ted Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Raimi "Ted Raimi") and long-time friend [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell"), _[American Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Gothic\_(1995\_TV\_series) "American Gothic (1995 TV series)")_, _[Cleopatra 2525](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra\_2525 "Cleopatra 2525")_, _[M.A.N.T.I.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.A.N.T.I.S. "M.A.N.T.I.S.")_, _[13: Fear Is Real](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13:\_Fear\_Is\_Real "13: Fear Is Real")_, _[Young Hercules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Hercules "Young Hercules")_, and _[Jack of All Trades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_of\_All\_Trades\_(TV\_series) "Jack of All Trades (TV series)")_. In 2008, Raimi executive-produced a syndicated TV series called _[Legend of the Seeker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend\_of\_the\_Seeker "Legend of the Seeker")_, based on [Terry Goodkind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Goodkind "Terry Goodkind")'s best-selling _[The Sword of Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sword\_of\_Truth "The Sword of Truth")_ fantasy series. He also executive produced the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz_(TV_channel) "Starz (TV channel)") original television series _[Spartacus: Blood and Sand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Blood\_and\_Sand "Spartacus: Blood and Sand")_, _[Spartacus: Gods of the Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Gods\_of\_the\_Arena "Spartacus: Gods of the Arena")_,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-51)_[Spartacus: Vengeance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Vengeance "Spartacus: Vengeance")_ and _[Spartacus: War of the Damned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_War\_of\_the\_Damned "Spartacus: War of the Damned")_. He directed the [pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") episode of _[Ash vs Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ash\_vs\_Evil\_Dead "Ash vs Evil Dead")_ for Starz.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-52)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 1993, Raimi married Gillian Greene, the daughter of Canadian actor [Lorne Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorne_Greene "Lorne Greene"). They have five children; their three eldest, daughter Emma Rose and sons Lorne and Henry, appeared as extras in _Drag Me to Hell_ and during the final battle in _Spider-Man 3_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-53) Greene filed for divorce on May 8, 2024, citing [irreconcilable differences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irreconcilable_differences "Irreconcilable differences").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-54) His daughter, Emma Raimi appeared in his 2026 film, _Send Help_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-55)

### Political donations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Political donations")]

In 1995, Raimi donated $450 to the campaign of then-[Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") Senator [Arlen Specter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlen_Specter "Arlen Specter"). In 2002, he donated $1,000 to [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") Senator [Barbara Boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Boxer "Barbara Boxer").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-56) During the [2004 election cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election"), Raimi donated $1,000 to Republican President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). Most recently, Raimi donated $2,950 to [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton")'s campaign early in the [2016 election cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-57)

**Samuel M. Raimi**[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-first-4) ([/ˈ r eɪ m i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_RAY-mee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born October 23, 1959) is an American filmmaker. He is best known for writing and directing the [_Evil Dead_ trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil_Dead "Evil Dead") (1981–1993) and directing the [_Spider-Man_ trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man_in_film#Sam_Raimi's_trilogy "Spider-Man in film") (2002–2007). He also directed _[Darkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkman "Darkman")_ (1990), _[The Quick and the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quick\_and\_the\_Dead\_(1995\_film) "The Quick and the Dead (1995 film)")_ (1995), _[A Simple Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Simple\_Plan\_(film) "A Simple Plan (film)")_ (1998), _[The Gift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gift\_(2000\_film) "The Gift (2000 film)")_ (2000), _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_ (2009), _[Oz the Great and Powerful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_the\_Great\_and\_Powerful "Oz the Great and Powerful")_ (2013), _[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_in\_the\_Multiverse\_of\_Madness "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness")_ (2022) and _[Send Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Send\_Help "Send Help")_ (2026).

His films are known for their highly dynamic visual style, inspired by comic books and slapstick comedy.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-6) He founded the production companies Renaissance Pictures in 1979 and [Ghost House Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_House_Pictures "Ghost House Pictures") in 2002. Raimi has also produced several successful television series, including _[Hercules: The Legendary Journeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hercules:\_The\_Legendary\_Journeys "Hercules: The Legendary Journeys")_ (1995–1997), its spin-off _[Xena: Warrior Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xena:\_Warrior\_Princess "Xena: Warrior Princess")_ (1995–2001), and _[Ash vs Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ash\_vs\_Evil\_Dead "Ash vs Evil Dead")_ (2015–2018) starring longtime friend and collaborator [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell") reprising his role in the _Evil Dead_ franchise.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Raimi was born on October 23, 1959, in [Royal Oak, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Oak,_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan"), a suburb of [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-TCM-1) His family was [Conservative Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Jewish "Conservative Jewish").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-7) He is a son of merchants Celia Barbara (née Abrams) (1929–2016) and Leonard Ronald Raimi (1926–2021).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-FilmRef-2) His ancestors were Jewish immigrants from Russia and Hungary.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-JewishJournal-March2012-8) His younger brother [Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Raimi "Ted Raimi") is an actor,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-9) and his older brother [Ivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Raimi "Ivan Raimi") is a screenwriter and physician.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-JewishJournal-March2012-8) His older sister, Andrea Raimi Rubin, is a court reporter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-10) Another older brother, Sander, died at 15 in an accidental drowning in [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"); Raimi has said that the trauma knitted the remaining family closer together and "colored everything he's done for the rest of his life."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-11) Raimi also mentioned that Sander first introduced him to _[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man")_, igniting his love for comics.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-:0-12)

Raimi graduated from [Groves High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groves_High_School_(Michigan) "Groves High School (Michigan)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-macomb-13) and later went on to attend [Michigan State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_University "Michigan State University") and later [Università Bocconi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bocconi_University "Bocconi University") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), Italy,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-15) where he studied English but left after three semesters to film _[The Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Dead "The Evil Dead")_.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Film")]

Raimi became fascinated with making films when his father brought a movie camera home one day. He began to make [Super 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_8_mm_film "Super 8 mm film") movies with his friend [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell"), whom he met in 1975. In college, he collaborated with his brother's roommate [Robert Tapert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Tapert "Robert Tapert") and Campbell to shoot _[Within the Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Within\_the\_Woods "Within the Woods")_ (1979), a 32-minute horror film which raised $375,000, as well as his debut feature film _[It's Murder!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Murder! "It's Murder!")_. During that time, he also shot the seven-minute short film _Clockwork_ (1979), starring [Scott Spiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Spiegel "Scott Spiegel") (who had appeared in _Within the Woods_) and Cheryl Guttridge.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-17) Through family, friends, and a network of investors, Raimi was able to finance production of the highly successful [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[The Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Evil\_Dead "The Evil Dead")_ (1981), which became a cult hit and effectively launched Raimi's career.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-18)

He began work on his third film _[Crimewave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimewave "Crimewave")_ (1985), which he co-wrote with the then-unknown [Coen brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coen_brothers "Coen brothers"), shortly after.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-19) Intended as a live-action comic book, the film was unsuccessful, partly due to unwanted studio intervention. Raimi then returned to the horror genre with the seminal _[Evil Dead II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil\_Dead\_II "Evil Dead II")_ (which added [slapstick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick "Slapstick") humor to the over-the-top horror, showcasing his love of the [Three Stooges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Stooges "Three Stooges")). With his brother [Ivan Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Raimi "Ivan Raimi") (and crediting himself as Celia Abrams), Sam Raimi also wrote _[Easy Wheels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easy\_Wheels "Easy Wheels")_ (1989), which parodied the [Outlaw biker film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_biker_film "Outlaw biker film") genre. A long-time comic book buff, he then attempted to adapt "[The Shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shadow "The Shadow")" into a movie but was unable to secure the rights, so he created his own superhero, _[Darkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkman "Darkman")_ (1990). The film was his first [major studio picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_film_studio "Major film studio"), and was commercially successful, spawning two sequels. Through it he was still able to secure funding for _Evil Dead III_, which was retitled _[Army of Darkness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army\_of\_Darkness "Army of Darkness")_ and largely steered away from horror towards [fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film") and [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film") elements. _Army of Darkness_, the final movie in the _Evil Dead_ trilogy, commercially underperformed, yet on video became a cult classic.

In the 1990s, Raimi moved into other genres, directing such films as the western _[The Quick and the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Quick\_and\_the\_Dead\_(1995\_film) "The Quick and the Dead (1995 film)")_ (starring [Sharon Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Stone "Sharon Stone") and [Gene Hackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Hackman "Gene Hackman")), the highly acclaimed crime thriller _[A Simple Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Simple\_Plan\_(film) "A Simple Plan (film)")_ (1998) (starring [Bill Paxton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Paxton "Bill Paxton") and [Billy Bob Thornton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Bob_Thornton "Billy Bob Thornton")), and the romantic drama _[For Love of the Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_Love\_of\_the\_Game\_(film) "For Love of the Game (film)")_ (1999) (starring [Kevin Costner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Costner "Kevin Costner")).

Raimi has frequently collaborated with [Joel and Ethan Coen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coen_brothers "Coen brothers"), beginning when Joel was one of the editors of _Evil Dead_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-20) The Coens co-wrote _Crimewave_ and _[The Hudsucker Proxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hudsucker\_Proxy "The Hudsucker Proxy")_ with Raimi in the mid-1980s (though _Hudsucker_ was not produced for almost a decade). Raimi made cameo appearances in _[Miller's Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miller's\_Crossing "Miller's Crossing")_, _The Hudsucker Proxy_, and with Joel Coen in _[Spies Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spies\_Like\_Us "Spies Like Us")_. The Coen brothers gave Raimi advice on shooting in snow for _A Simple Plan_, based on their experiences with _[Fargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo\_(1996\_film) "Fargo (1996 film)")_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-21)

Raimi has worked in front of the camera in _[The Stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Stand\_(1994\_miniseries) "The Stand (1994 miniseries)")_ as a dimwitted hitman, [John Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carpenter "John Carpenter")'s _[Body Bags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body\_Bags\_(film) "Body Bags (film)")_ as a murdered gas station attendant, and _[Indian Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Summer\_(1993\_film) "Indian Summer (1993 film)")_ in what is perhaps his biggest role as a bumbling assistant to [Alan Arkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Arkin "Alan Arkin"). The film was written by his childhood friend, writer-director [Mike Binder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Binder "Mike Binder"), and shot at the camp that they both attended when they were younger.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_%282%29.jpg/250px-Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Raimi_by_David_Shankbone_(2).jpg)

Raimi in 2007

Raimi achieved great critical and commercial success with the [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)")_[Spider-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_(2002\_film) "Spider-Man (2002 film)")_ (2002), which was adapted from the comic book series [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man"). The movie grossed over US$800 million worldwide, spawning two sequels: _[Spider-Man 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_2 "Spider-Man 2")_ and _[Spider-Man 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man\_3 "Spider-Man 3")_, both directed by Raimi and each grossing approximately $800 million. After the completion of the third _Spider-Man_ film, he planned on producing two more sequels (although [Sony Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures "Sony Pictures") planned three sequels) but could not find a satisfactory script.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-rolling_stone-22) In 2022, reflecting on _Spider-Man 3_, Raimi told _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_: "It was a very painful experience for me. I wanted to make a Spider-Man movie to redeem myself for that. [The aborted] _Spider-Man 4_ — that was really what that was about. I wanted to go out on a high note. I didn't want to just make another one that pretty much worked. I had a really high standard in my mind. And I didn't think I could get that script to the level that I was hoping for by that start date."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-:0-12) He, along with [Marc Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Webb "Marc Webb"), were both brought on as creative consultants for [Marvel Studios'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios")_[Spider-Man: No Way Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_No\_Way\_Home "Spider-Man: No Way Home")_, directed by [Jon Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Watts "Jon Watts").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-23)

Raimi produced the entire English-language [_The Grudge_ franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grudge_(film_series) "The Grudge (film series)"), based on the original Japanese films. On December 11, 2006, the website SuperHeroHype reported that director Sam Raimi and Michael Uslan would co-produce a new film version of _[The Shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shadow "The Shadow")_ for [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-24) On October 16, 2007, Raimi stated that: "I don't have any news on _The Shadow_ at this time, except that the company that I have with Josh Donen, my producing partner, we've got the rights to _The Shadow_. I love the character very much and we're trying to work on a story that'll do justice to the character."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-26) According to _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_, Raimi had expressed an interest in directing a film version of _[The Hobbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hobbit "The Hobbit")_, the prequel to the _[Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lord\_of\_the\_Rings "The Lord of the Rings")_ trilogy.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-27) In 2008, it was reported [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro") would direct with [Peter Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Jackson "Peter Jackson") as the executive producer, though Jackson ultimately directed [_The Hobbit_ film series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hobbit_(film_series) "The Hobbit (film series)"). In 2008, it was reported Raimi might direct _By Any Means Necessary_, the next film based on the "Jack Ryan" CIA character created by [Tom Clancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Clancy "Tom Clancy") for [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-28) Disney also approached him to direct _[W.I.T.C.H.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W.I.T.C.H. "W.I.T.C.H."): The Movie_, based on the popular comic.

Raimi directed the horror film _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_, released in 2009 to critical acclaim.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-29) Blizzard Entertainment announced on July 22, 2009, that Raimi would be directing a film adaptation of the _[Warcraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warcraft "Warcraft")_ video game series,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-30) but at the 2012 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con"), it was revealed that he would not be the director.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-31)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg/250px-Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drag_Me_to_Hell_ComicCon_panel.jpg)

Raimi (far left) at the _[Drag Me to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag\_Me\_to\_Hell "Drag Me to Hell")_ film discussion panel at the 2008 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

In 2009, it was reported Raimi would produce the British [supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural "Supernatural")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_film "Thriller film")_Refuge_, which would be directed by [Corin Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corin_Hardy "Corin Hardy") and published by [Mandate Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_Pictures "Mandate Pictures"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-32) and the remake of the Danish thriller _[The Substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Substitute\_(2007\_film) "The Substitute (2007 film)")_, which would be directed by [Scott Derrickson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Derrickson "Scott Derrickson"), under his new label Spooky Pictures.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-33) In 2010, it was reported he would produce the British thriller flick _Burst 3D_ with his company [Ghost House Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_House_Pictures "Ghost House Pictures"), directed by [Neil Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Marshall "Neil Marshall").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-34)

Raimi directed _[Oz the Great and Powerful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_the\_Great\_and\_Powerful "Oz the Great and Powerful")_, which was released on March 8, 2013, by [Walt Disney Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Pictures "Walt Disney Pictures") and grossed $493 million worldwide.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-36) He said he would not be directing the planned sequel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-signed-sequel-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-noraimi-38)

Raimi, along with Bruce Campbell and [Rob Tapert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Tapert "Rob Tapert"), produced 2013's _[Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil\_Dead\_(2013\_film) "Evil Dead (2013 film)"),_ a remake of Raimi's original film. First-time feature filmmaker [Fede Álvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fede_%C3%81lvarez "Fede Álvarez") wrote and directed, and [Diablo Cody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diablo_Cody "Diablo Cody") was also brought in to revise/rewrite the script.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-39) Raimi confirmed plans to write _Evil Dead 4_ with his brother; it was later specified that this film would be _Army of Darkness 2_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-40) Álvarez revealed that Raimi would direct the sequel to _Army of Darkness_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-41) However, in a 2014 interview, [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell") announced that _Army of Darkness 2_ is not happening, saying "It's all internet b.s. There's no reality whatsoever. These random comments slip out of either my mouth, or Sam Raimi's mouth, next thing you know, we're making a sequel."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-42)

Raimi speaking at the 2014 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

On February 26, 2016, it was confirmed that Raimi was attached to direct the upcoming film _World War 3_ for [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") The film would be based on a possible future inspired by the book _[The Next 100 Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Next\_100\_Years "The Next 100 Years")_ by [George Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Friedman "George Friedman").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-43) On February 16, 2017, it was reported that Raimi would be directing a thriller about the [Bermuda Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_Triangle "Bermuda Triangle") for [Skydance Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skydance_Media "Skydance Media"), with the script being written by Doug Miro and Carlo Bernard.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-44) By January 29, 2018, Raimi was set to direct the first in the movie adaptations of [Patrick Rothfuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Rothfuss "Patrick Rothfuss")'s [Kingkiller Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kingkiller_Chronicle "The Kingkiller Chronicle") series, _[The Name of the Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Name\_of\_the\_Wind "The Name of the Wind")_, with Rothfuss and [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") serving as executive producers.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-45)

On February 5, 2020, it was announced that Raimi was in talks with [Marvel Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios") to direct _[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_in\_the\_Multiverse\_of\_Madness "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness")_,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-46) and Raimi confirmed his involvement in April 2020.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-47) This marked Raimi's return to the superhero film genre after more than 15 years following _Spider-Man 3_ in 2007 and his first feature film directorial effort since 2013's _Oz the Great and Powerful._[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-48)

Raimi next directed the horror-thriller film _[Send Help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Send\_Help "Send Help")_, starring [Rachel McAdams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_McAdams "Rachel McAdams") and [Dylan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_O'Brien "Dylan O'Brien").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-49) The film was released in theatres by [20th Century Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Studios "20th Century Studios") on January 30, 2026.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-50)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Television")]

In addition to film, Raimi has worked in television, producing such series as _[Hercules: The Legendary Journeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hercules:\_The\_Legendary\_Journeys "Hercules: The Legendary Journeys")_ and its [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_(media) "Spin-off (media)")_[Xena: Warrior Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xena:\_Warrior\_Princess "Xena: Warrior Princess")_, both featuring his younger brother [Ted Raimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Raimi "Ted Raimi") and long-time friend [Bruce Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Campbell "Bruce Campbell"), _[American Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Gothic\_(1995\_TV\_series) "American Gothic (1995 TV series)")_, _[Cleopatra 2525](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra\_2525 "Cleopatra 2525")_, _[M.A.N.T.I.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.A.N.T.I.S. "M.A.N.T.I.S.")_, _[13: Fear Is Real](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13:\_Fear\_Is\_Real "13: Fear Is Real")_, _[Young Hercules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Hercules "Young Hercules")_, and _[Jack of All Trades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack\_of\_All\_Trades\_(TV\_series) "Jack of All Trades (TV series)")_. In 2008, Raimi executive-produced a syndicated TV series called _[Legend of the Seeker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legend\_of\_the\_Seeker "Legend of the Seeker")_, based on [Terry Goodkind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Goodkind "Terry Goodkind")'s best-selling _[The Sword of Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sword\_of\_Truth "The Sword of Truth")_ fantasy series. He also executive produced the [Starz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starz_(TV_channel) "Starz (TV channel)") original television series _[Spartacus: Blood and Sand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Blood\_and\_Sand "Spartacus: Blood and Sand")_, _[Spartacus: Gods of the Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Gods\_of\_the\_Arena "Spartacus: Gods of the Arena")_,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-51)_[Spartacus: Vengeance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_Vengeance "Spartacus: Vengeance")_ and _[Spartacus: War of the Damned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartacus:\_War\_of\_the\_Damned "Spartacus: War of the Damned")_. He directed the [pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") episode of _[Ash vs Evil Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ash\_vs\_Evil\_Dead "Ash vs Evil Dead")_ for Starz.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-52)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 1993, Raimi married Gillian Greene, the daughter of Canadian actor [Lorne Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorne_Greene "Lorne Greene"). They have five children; their three eldest, daughter Emma Rose and sons Lorne and Henry, appeared as extras in _Drag Me to Hell_ and during the final battle in _Spider-Man 3_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-53) Greene filed for divorce on May 8, 2024, citing [irreconcilable differences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irreconcilable_differences "Irreconcilable differences").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-54) His daughter, Emma Raimi appeared in his 2026 film, _Send Help_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-55)

### Political donations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Raimi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Political donations")]

In 1995, Raimi donated $450 to the campaign of then-[Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") Senator [Arlen Specter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlen_Specter "Arlen Specter"). In 2002, he donated $1,000 to [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") Senator [Barbara Boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Boxer "Barbara Boxer").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-56) During the [2004 election cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election"), Raimi donated $1,000 to Republican President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). Most recently, Raimi donated $2,950 to [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton")'s campaign early in the [2016 election cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Raimi#cite_note-57)
